focus: Fixed-exposure filmic display transform, highlight rolloff, shadow-toe separation and grazing-angle texture clarity for the 4K live-action target.

implementationCommits.message: Add deterministic cinematic camera display transform
Add cinematic exposure and tonemap QA pass
Integrate cinematic transform with physical lighting pipeline
Preserve HDR precision through filmic rolloff

verification.gitComparison: startHead -> implementationHead is ahead by 6, behind by 0
verification.packageManifest: No SRP dependencies declared; benchmark remains on Built-in Render Pipeline contract.

implementationReadiness.reason: Do not award readiness for visual code that has not compiled in Unity 6000.3.0f1; the remaining blocker is still real runtime verification.

expectedVisualScoreImpact.lightingShadowsReflections: Potentially high: HDR peaks now pass through a deterministic shoulder instead of relying on hard display clipping.
expectedVisualScoreImpact.cinematicImageQuality: Potentially high: fixed cross-view exposure, restrained saturation/contrast and shadow toe establish a stable filmic display baseline.
expectedVisualScoreImpact.textureMicrodetail: Potentially modest: forced anisotropic filtering improves grazing-angle material sampling without post sharpening.
expectedVisualScoreImpact.temporalStability: Potentially positive: no auto exposure or dynamic resolution is allowed in benchmark capture, reducing cross-view exposure pumping and pixel-scale instability.

criticalFailProtectionAdded: No bloom/sharpening/chromatic aberration/vignette/local-contrast masking in the benchmark filmic pass.
HDR precision is retained until after exposure and shoulder compression.
Linear color space and fixed benchmark exposure are enforced by QA.
Dynamic resolution is rejected for pixel-exact 4K evidence.
nextBlocker: Unity 6000.3.0f1 compile/import plus actual 3840x2160 hero/oblique/grazing capture. Until that exists, Visual Fidelity remains unscored. If runtime remains unavailable, the next safe score-oriented implementation target is shadow/contact quality and thin-geometry anti-aliasing stability rather than additional grading.
externalTechnicalBasis: Unity 6 Built-in Render Pipeline supports OnRenderImage image filters on Camera components.
Camera.Render executes attached image filters during manual capture.
Unity HDR camera paths use floating-point HDR buffers before display mapping.
